target_customer: Software development teams that want a second pair of expert eyes on every pull request
problem: Code review is slow and inconsistent inside small teams, and good reviewers are scarce. PullRequest combined static analysis with a network of on-demand human reviewers.
business_model: Subscription per reviewed pull request or team plan, with a paid network of freelance reviewers

founders.name: Lyal Avery
founders.background_notes: YC page lists only Avery and gives no background. One aggregator (Golden) names Tyler Mann and Patrick Barsallo as further co-founders; not confirmed by YC or company sources, so not listed.

technical_complexity.rationale: Integrations with GitHub, Bitbucket and GitLab plus a reviewer marketplace and routing are standard engineering; the hard part was recruiting and vetting reviewers, not the software.

defensibility.rationale: The reviewer network and customer integrations helped, but the model was easy to copy by any consultancy or freelance marketplace, and the core review work is human labor.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No platform copied the human review model as far as sources show. Security vendor HackerOne bought the company in April 2022 to add source code reviewers to its community.

market_need_then: Launch coverage in August 2017 described teams needing outside experts to check bugs, security, standards and performance in code before it ships. The company built it as extra eyes, not a replacement for internal review.

branding.domain_note: Company used pullrequest.com; no purchase story found.

rebrands.why: Folded into the acquirer's brand after the April 2022 acquisition; the site now announces the rename to HackerOne Code (month not stated).

brand_strength.rationale: The name is the common developer term for the thing it reviews, which made it self-explanatory but generic. No sources show mascot, merch or brand press beyond product launch coverage.

outcome_analysis: PullRequest raised a $2.3M seed in December 2017 and an $8M Series A in April 2018 led by Gradient Ventures, bought the developer marketplace Moonlight in 2020, and was acquired by HackerOne in April 2022 at an undisclosed price. The exit came as a strategic fit for a security vendor rather than from a large standalone business. The product was later rebranded under HackerOne.
notes: CB Insights lists about $12.82M raised versus roughly $10.3M from the two rounds, so earlier or later amounts may be missing; coverage is partial. Competitor search found no dated 2017 competitor named by a contemporaneous source, so the list is empty. Founder education and prior employers were not found. Price of the HackerOne deal was undisclosed.
